title: CharacterBody2D get_position_delta returns initial transform at first run
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in Godot Engine v4.4.stable.official [4c311cbee]. ### System information Godot v4.4.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.3.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M1 Max - Apple M1 Max (10 threads) ### Issue description CharacterBody2D.get_position_delta() is documented so that it should return the travel (position delta) that occurred **during the last call** to move_and_slide(). However, if it is called before move_and_slide(), it returns the distance, that was defined by initial Transform -> Position property of the CharacterBody2D. The CharacterBody2D.get_position_delta() should return probably Vector2.ZERO if move_and_slide() has not been called yet. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create simple 2D project, create 2D scene. 2. Insert nodes for CharacterBody2D (and a StaticBody2D for instance) alongside with their collision shapes. 3. Transform the CharacterBody2D so its initial position.y is significantly higher than 0.0 (i. e. 1000). 4. Add a default basic movement script to CharacterBody2D. 5. In _physics(delta: float) function measure the distance fallen by calling get_position_delta(), print it to the console. 6. The first get_position_delta() call (even before move_and_slide() is called) returns initial transform coordinates. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [get_position_delta_Minimal_Project.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19309332/get_position_delta_Minimal_Project.zip)
